passages.text: In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat’s reign over Judah, Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twelve years.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was the son of Ahab.
Jehoram became king of Israel.
Jehoram began to reign in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat’s rule over Judah.
Jehoram ruled in Samaria.
Jehoram reigned for twelve years.
passages.original: וִיהוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן־ אַחְאָ֗ב מָלַ֤ךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה עֶשְׂרֵ֔ה לִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ שְׁתֵּים־ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as his father and mother had done. He removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was the son of Ahab.
Jehoram became king of Israel.
Jehoram did evil in the sight of the LORD.
He did not do as much evil as his father and mother.
Jehoram removed the sacred pillar of Baal.
His father had made this pillar.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה רַ֕ק לֹ֥א כְאָבִ֖יו וּכְאִמּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֙סַר֙ אֶת־ מַצְּבַ֣ת הַבַּ֔עַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, he clung to the sins that Jeroboam son of Nebat had caused Israel to commit; he did not turn away from them.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was king of Israel.
He was the son of Ahab.
He ruled in Samaria.
He did not follow the LORD fully.
He held on to the sins of Jeroboam.
Jeroboam was the son of Nebat.
Jeroboam led Israel into sin.
Jehoram did not turn away from these sins.
passages.original: רַ֠ק בְּחַטֹּ֞אות יָרָבְעָ֧ם בֶּֽן־ נְבָ֛ט אֲשֶׁר־ הֶחֱטִ֥יא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דָּבֵ֑ק לֹא־ סָ֖ר מִמֶּֽנָּה׃ס

passages.text: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he would render to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
passages.sermon:
Mesha was the king of Moab.
Mesha bred sheep.
Mesha gave gifts to the king of Israel.
He gave one hundred thousand lambs.
He also gave the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
passages.original: וּמֵישַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ־ מוֹאָ֖ב הָיָ֣ה נֹקֵ֑ד וְהֵשִׁ֤יב לְמֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאָה־ אֶ֣לֶף כָּרִ֔ים וּמֵ֥אָה אֶ֖לֶף אֵילִ֥ים צָֽמֶר׃

passages.text: But after the death of Ahab, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Ahab died.
The king of Moab ruled Moab.
After Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled.
The king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י כְּמ֣וֹת אַחְאָ֑ב וַיִּפְשַׁ֥ע מֶֽלֶךְ־ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּמֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So at that time King Jehoram set out from Samaria and mobilized all Israel.
passages.sermon:
King Jehoram ruled Israel.
He lived in Samaria.
On that day, King Jehoram left Samaria.
He called together all the people of Israel.
He gathered them for action.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֞א הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא מִשֹּׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּפְקֹ֖ד אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And he sent a message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?” “I will go,” replied Jehoshaphat. “I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.”
passages.sermon:
King Jehoram ruled Israel.
The king of Moab rebelled against King Jehoram.
King Jehoram sent a message to Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
King Jehoram said, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me.”
He asked Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to fight against Moab?”
Jehoshaphat answered, “I will go.”
Jehoshaphat said, “I am like you.”
He said, “My people are your people.”
He said, “My horses are your horses.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֡לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אֶל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֨ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע בִּ֔י הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֛י אֶל־ מוֹאָ֖ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶעֱלֶ֔ה כָּמ֧וֹנִי כָמ֛וֹךָ כְּעַמִּ֥י כְעַמֶּ֖ךָ כְּסוּסַ֥י כְּסוּסֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then he asked, “Which way shall we go up?” “By way of the Desert of Edom,” replied Joram.
passages.sermon:
King Jehoram led Israel.
He asked a question.
He said, “Which way shall we go?”
Joram answered.
He said, “By way of the Desert of Edom.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵי־ זֶ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ נַעֲלֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and after they had traveled a roundabout route for seven days, they had no water for their army or for their animals.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel went out.
The king of Judah went with him.
The king of Edom also went with them.
These three kings traveled together.
They took a roundabout route.
They traveled for seven days.
They had no water for their army.
They had no water for their animals.
passages.original: וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וּמֶֽלֶך־ יְהוּדָה֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֔וֹם וַיָּסֹ֕בּוּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וְלֹא־ הָיָ֨ה מַ֧יִם לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֛ה וְלַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: “Alas,” said the king of Israel, “for the LORD has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab!”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He said, “Alas!”
The LORD has called these three kings.
The LORD will give these three kings into the hand of Moab.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲהָ֕הּ כִּֽי־ קָרָ֣א יְהוָ֗ה לִשְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־ מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here? Let us inquire of the LORD through him.” And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He spoke to the other kings.
He asked a question.
He said, “Is there a prophet of the LORD here?”
He wanted to seek guidance from the LORD.
He said, “Let us inquire of the LORD through him.”
A servant of the king of Israel answered.
The servant said, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here.”
Elisha served Elijah.
Elisha used to pour water on Elijah’s hands.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֤ה נָבִיא֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְנִדְרְשָׁ֥ה אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה מֵאוֹת֑וֹ וַ֠יַּעַן אֶחָ֞ד מֵעַבְדֵ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר פֹּ֚ה אֱלִישָׁ֣ע בֶּן־ שָׁפָ֔ט אֲשֶׁר־ יָ֥צַק מַ֖יִם עַל־ יְדֵ֥י אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Jehoshaphat affirmed, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He spoke about Elisha.
Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with Elisha.”
The king of Israel was present.
Jehoshaphat was present.
The king of Edom was present.
These three kings went down to Elisha.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט יֵ֥שׁ אוֹת֖וֹ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּרְד֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו מֶ֧לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט וּמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Elisha, however, said to the king of Israel, “What have we to do with each other? Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother!” “No,” replied the king of Israel, “for it is the LORD who has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of the LORD.
Elisha spoke to the king of Israel.
Elisha said, “What do you and I have in common?”
Elisha told the king, “Go to the prophets of your father.”
Elisha also said, “Go to the prophets of your mother.”
The king of Israel answered Elisha.
The king said, “No.”
The king explained, “The LORD has called these three kings together.”
The king said, “The LORD will give them into the hand of Moab.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֜ע אֶל־ מֶ֤לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַה־ לִּ֣י וָלָ֔ךְ לֵ֚ךְ אֶל־ נְבִיאֵ֣י אָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶל־ נְבִיאֵ֖י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַ֗ל כִּֽי־ קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ לִשְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לָתֵ֥ת אוֹתָ֖ם בְּיַד־ מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: Then Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, were it not for my regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or acknowledge you.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of the LORD of Hosts.
Elisha spoke to the king of Israel.
Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand."
Elisha respected Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah.
Elisha said, "If Jehoshaphat king of Judah were not here, I would not pay attention to you."
Elisha said, "I would not even look at you or see you."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֗ע חַי־ יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָמַ֣דְתִּי לְפָנָ֔יו כִּ֗י לוּלֵ֛י פְּנֵ֛י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י נֹשֵׂ֑א אִם־ אַבִּ֥יט אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְאִם־ אֶרְאֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: But now, bring me a harpist.” And while the harpist played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha and he said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of the LORD.
Elisha spoke to the people.
Elisha said, “Now bring me a harpist.”
They brought a harpist.
The harpist played music.
While the harpist played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha.
The LORD gave Elisha a message.
Elisha said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD said, “Dig this valley full of ditches.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה קְחוּ־ לִ֣י מְנַגֵּ֑ן וְהָיָה֙ כְּנַגֵּ֣ן הַֽמְנַגֵּ֔ן וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֖יו יַד־ יְהוָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עָשֹׂ֛ה הַנַּ֥חַל הַזֶּ֖ה גֵּבִ֥ים׀ גֵּבִֽים׃

passages.text: For the LORD says, ‘You will not see wind or rain, but the valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you and your cattle and your animals.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD says this:
You will not see wind.
You will not see rain.
The valley will become full of water.
You will drink this water.
Your cattle will drink this water.
Your other animals will drink this water.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לֹֽא־ תִרְא֥וּ ר֙וּחַ֙ וְלֹֽא־ תִרְא֣וּ גֶ֔שֶׁם וְהַנַּ֥חַל הַה֖וּא יִמָּ֣לֵא מָ֑יִם וּשְׁתִיתֶ֛ם אַתֶּ֥ם וּמִקְנֵיכֶ֖ם וּֽבְהֶמְתְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: This is a simple matter in the sight of the LORD, and He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful.
Nothing is too hard for Him.
The LORD sees this as a simple thing.
The LORD will give you victory over Moab.
The LORD will put the Moabites into your hand.
passages.original: וְנָקַ֥ל זֹ֖את בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶת־ מוֹאָ֖ב בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And you shall attack every fortified city and every city of importance. You shall cut down every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God told them to attack Moab.
You must attack every city with strong walls.
You must attack every important city.
You must cut down every good tree.
You must stop up every spring of water.
You must ruin every good field with stones.
passages.original: וְהִכִּיתֶ֞ם כָּל־ עִ֤יר מִבְצָר֙ וְכָל־ עִ֣יר מִבְח֔וֹר וְכָל־ עֵ֥ץ טוֹב֙ תַּפִּ֔ילוּ וְכָל־ מַעְיְנֵי־ מַ֖יִם תִּסְתֹּ֑מוּ וְכֹל֙ הַחֶלְקָ֣ה הַטּוֹבָ֔ה תַּכְאִ֖בוּ בָּאֲבָנִֽים׃

passages.text: The next morning, at the time of the morning sacrifice, water suddenly flowed from the direction of Edom and filled the land.
passages.sermon:
God acted in the morning.
The morning sacrifice was taking place.
Water began to flow.
The water came from the direction of Edom.
The water filled the land.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ כַּעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־ מַ֥יִם בָּאִ֖ים מִדֶּ֣רֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א הָאָ֖רֶץ אֶת־ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. So all who could bear arms, young and old, were summoned and stationed at the border.
passages.sermon:
The Moabites were a nation.
They heard news.
They heard that enemy kings were coming.
The kings were coming to fight against them.
Every Moabite who could fight was called.
This included both young and old men.
They gathered all who could wear armor.
They brought them to the border.
They stationed them there to defend Moab.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מוֹאָב֙ שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּֽי־ עָל֥וּ הַמְּלָכִ֖ים לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בָּ֑ם וַיִּצָּעֲק֗וּ מִכֹּ֨ל חֹגֵ֤ר חֲגֹרָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה וַיַּעַמְד֖וּ עַֽל־ הַגְּבֽוּל׃

passages.text: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, and it looked as red as blood to the Moabites across the way.
passages.sermon:
The Moabites were a nation living near Israel.
The Moabites woke up early in the morning.
The sun rose and shone on the water.
The Moabites looked at the water from a distance.
The water appeared red to the Moabites.
The water looked as red as blood.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ זָרְחָ֣ה עַל־ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּרְא֨וּ מוֹאָ֥ב מִנֶּ֛גֶד אֶת־ הַמַּ֖יִם אֲדֻמִּ֥ים כַּדָּֽם׃

passages.text: “This is blood!” they exclaimed. “The kings have clashed swords and slaughtered one another. Now to the plunder, Moab!”
passages.sermon:
The Moabites saw the water.
They saw that the water looked red.
They thought the water was blood.
The Moabites said, “This is blood.”
They believed the kings had fought each other.
They said, “The kings have destroyed one another.”
They said, “Each king has struck down his companion.”
They called out, “Now, Moab, go and take the plunder.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ דָּ֣ם זֶ֔ה הָחֳרֵ֤ב נֶֽחֶרְבוּ֙ הַמְּלָכִ֔ים וַיַּכּ֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְעַתָּ֥ה לַשָּׁלָ֖ל מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and attacked them, and they fled before them. So the Israelites invaded their land and struck down the Moabites.
passages.sermon:
The Moabites came to the camp of Israel.
The Israelites stood up.
The Israelites attacked the Moabites.
The Moabites ran away from the Israelites.
The Israelites entered the land of Moab.
The Israelites struck down the Moabites.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ֮ אֶל־ מַחֲנֵ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּ אֶת־ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבוֹ בָ֔הּ וְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־ מוֹאָֽב׃

passages.text: They destroyed the cities, and each man threw stones on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up every spring and cut down every good tree. Only Kir-haraseth was left with stones in place, but men with slings surrounded it and attacked it as well.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites attacked the land of Moab.
They destroyed the cities.
Each man threw stones onto every good field.
They covered the fields with stones.
They stopped up every spring of water.
They cut down every good tree.
Only the city of Kir-haraseth remained with its stones in place.
Men with slings surrounded Kir-haraseth.
They attacked the city with their slings.
passages.original: וְהֶעָרִ֣ים יַהֲרֹ֡סוּ וְכָל־ חֶלְקָ֣ה ט֠וֹבָה יַשְׁלִ֨יכוּ אִישׁ־ אַבְנ֜וֹ וּמִלְא֗וּהָ וְכָל־ מַעְיַן־ מַ֤יִם יִסְתֹּ֙מוּ֙ וְכָל־ עֵֽץ־ ט֣וֹב יַפִּ֔ילוּ עַד־ הִשְׁאִ֧יר אֲבָנֶ֛יהָ בַּקִּ֖יר חֲרָ֑שֶׂת וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ הַקַּלָּעִ֖ים וַיַּכּֽוּהָ׃

passages.text: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not prevail.
passages.sermon:
The king of Moab saw the battle was too strong for him.
He took seven hundred men with swords.
He tried to break through to the king of Edom.
They could not succeed.
passages.original: וַיַּרְא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֔ב כִּֽי־ חָזַ֥ק מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֣ח א֠וֹתוֹ שְׁבַע־ מֵא֨וֹת אִ֜ישׁ שֹׁ֣לֵֽף חֶ֗רֶב לְהַבְקִ֛יעַ אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ אֱד֖וֹם וְלֹ֥א יָכֹֽלוּ׃

passages.text: So he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. And there was great fury against the Israelites, so they withdrew and returned to their own land.
passages.sermon:
The king of Moab saw that he was losing the battle.
He took his firstborn son.
This son was supposed to rule after him.
The king offered his son as a burnt offering.
He did this on the city wall.
Great anger came against Israel.
The Israelites left him.
They returned to their own land.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֶת־ בְּנ֨וֹ הַבְּכ֜וֹר אֲשֶׁר־ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֗יו וַיַּעֲלֵ֤הוּ עֹלָה֙ עַל־ הַ֣חֹמָ֔ה וַיְהִ֥י קֶצֶף־ גָּד֖וֹל עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃פ
